alphabet.name: ანი
alphabet.sound: a as in “father”, but short. Georgian vowels are never long and never glide.
alphabet.mnemonic: Small hook with a belly below – the simplest, plainest letter: a, the very first one.

alphabet.name: ბანი
alphabet.sound: b, always voiced – also at the end of a word.
alphabet.mnemonic: Round belly below, curl on top: a baby with a curl of hair.

alphabet.name: განი
alphabet.sound: g as in “go”, always voiced – never like the g in “gem”.
alphabet.mnemonic: Belly with a stalk rolled up on the left – like a twisted Latin g.

alphabet.name: დონი
alphabet.sound: d as in “day”, always voiced, also at the end of a word.
alphabet.mnemonic: Loop at the top left, an arch, tail swinging down to the right – a dragon in flight (d for dragon).

alphabet.name: ენი
alphabet.sound: open e as in “bed” – never the gliding “ay” of “day”.
alphabet.mnemonic: Like a mirrored C with a descender – an ear asking “eh?”.

alphabet.name: ვინი
alphabet.sound: roughly English v as in “van”. After consonants often almost like English w.
alphabet.mnemonic: A 3 hanging down (descender). Careful: the whole “3 family” ვ კ პ ჰ looks similar.

alphabet.name: ზენი
alphabet.sound: z as in “zoo” – a voiced s.
alphabet.mnemonic: Like ბ, but with a double wave on top – the wave is the zigzag of the Z.

alphabet.name: თანი
alphabet.sound: aspirated t as in “top” – a little puff of air follows.
alphabet.mnemonic: Two round humps side by side – a camel: t for two humps.

alphabet.name: ინი
alphabet.sound: i like the ee in “meet”, but short.
alphabet.mnemonic: Almost closed circle, open at the top left – a hedgehog curling up.

alphabet.name: კანი
alphabet.sound: Ejective: k without a puff of air, with the larynx closed – sounds like a short, hard click. Partner of ქ.
alphabet.mnemonic: Narrow 3 with a curled foot – short and clipped like the hard k'.

alphabet.name: ლასი
alphabet.sound: l; before a, o, u somewhat “dark” like the l in “full” (back of the tongue raised).
alphabet.mnemonic: Waves with a long tail to the bottom left – a lasso (l for lasso).

alphabet.name: მანი
alphabet.sound: m as in English.
alphabet.mnemonic: Round belly with a stroke hanging over to the right at the top – a man in a cap (m for man).

alphabet.name: ნარი
alphabet.sound: n as in English.
alphabet.mnemonic: Looks like a 6 – but it is an n.

alphabet.name: ონი
alphabet.sound: o as in British “hot”, a little rounder – never the gliding “oh” of “go”.
alphabet.mnemonic: A hump with a curled end on the right – like an earlobe.

alphabet.name: პარი
alphabet.sound: Ejective: p without a puff of air, with the larynx closed. Partner of ფ.
alphabet.mnemonic: Like კ with a loop on top – the pompom on a hat (p for pompom).

alphabet.name: ჟანი
alphabet.sound: voiced sh like the s in “measure” or “vision”.
alphabet.mnemonic: Like ე with a little crown on top – the soft “zh” of French “journal”.

alphabet.name: რაე
alphabet.sound: tapped or rolled r with the tip of the tongue (as in Spanish or Scottish English) – never the English r where the tongue does not touch, and never silent as in British “car”.
alphabet.mnemonic: An arch whose leg runs down on the left – an umbrella held at an angle (r for rain).

alphabet.name: სანი
alphabet.sound: always a voiceless s as in “sun” – never the z sound of “is” or “rose”.
alphabet.mnemonic: Like a U with the left arm raised – a bowl with a handle (s for saucepan).

alphabet.name: ტარი
alphabet.sound: Ejective: t without a puff of air, with the larynx closed. Partner of თ.
alphabet.mnemonic: Like ი with a knot on top – a teapot with a lid knob (t for teapot). Knot = hard (ejective).

alphabet.name: უნი
alphabet.sound: u like the oo in “food”, but short.
alphabet.mnemonic: Small hook on top, big belly below – a U-shaped sack hanging down.

alphabet.name: ფარი
alphabet.sound: aspirated p as in “pot” – CAREFUL: not an f, even though it is on the f key!
alphabet.mnemonic: Like უ with an extra loop on top – the “puff” sound: the loop is the breath.

alphabet.name: ქანი
alphabet.sound: aspirated k as in “kit”.
alphabet.mnemonic: Like ე with a small cross-stroke on the left – the k with breath.

alphabet.name: ღანი
alphabet.sound: voiced, rubbed r at the back of the throat – close to the French r in “Paris”, only rubbed more strongly.
alphabet.mnemonic: Like დ, but the loop sits lower – the sound also sits lower in the throat (a gargled r).

alphabet.name: ყარი
alphabet.sound: Ejective far back: like კ, but made at the uvula – a deep, hard click in the throat. The hardest sound; many speakers say it as an ejective kh [χʼ].
alphabet.mnemonic: Looks like a Latin y – but sounds completely different: q', deep in the throat.

alphabet.name: შინი
alphabet.sound: sh as in “shoe”.
alphabet.mnemonic: Like მ with an extra wave on top – more waves = more rushing noise: “sh”.

alphabet.name: ჩინი
alphabet.sound: aspirated ch as in “church”.
alphabet.mnemonic: Like a slanted R / h with two arches on top – “ch” with breath.

alphabet.name: ცანი
alphabet.sound: aspirated ts as in “cats” – also at the start of a word.
alphabet.mnemonic: Looks like a c with a hook – and sounds like the ts in “cats”.

alphabet.name: ძილი
alphabet.sound: voiced dz as in “kids” or “adze”.
alphabet.mnemonic: Looks like the symbol ∂ (belly below, stalk bending left) – voiced dz.

alphabet.name: წილი
alphabet.sound: Ejective: ts without a puff of air, with the larynx closed. Partner of ც.
alphabet.mnemonic: A pointed V with a hook at the top left – sharp and hard like the sound ts'.

alphabet.name: ჭარი
alphabet.sound: Ejective: ch without a puff of air, with the larynx closed. Partner of ჩ.
alphabet.mnemonic: Like ქ with an extra cross – “crossed = hard”: ejective ch'.

alphabet.name: ხანი
alphabet.sound: kh like the ch in Scottish “loch” or German “Bach” – rough, far back. Never a plain k or h.
alphabet.mnemonic: Like ნ with a little flag at the top left – “kh” as in “loch”.

alphabet.name: ჯანი
alphabet.sound: j as in “jungle” or “jam”.
alphabet.mnemonic: An ornate X – unique, hard to confuse: “j” as in “jungle”.

alphabet.name: ჰაე
alphabet.sound: h as in “house”. Rare, mainly in ჰო (ho, “yes”).
alphabet.mnemonic: A 3 with a flat lid on top – the 3 wears a hat (h for hat).

lessons.title: The five vowels and m, n, l, s
lessons.body:
## What this is about

Georgian has its own alphabet, **Mkhedruli** (მხედრული). Good to know up front:

- **One letter = one sound**, always. What you read is what you say. No silent letters, no exceptions – very unlike English spelling.
- **No capital and small letters.**
- Only **five vowels**, all **short and pure**: ა a · ე e · ი i · ო o · უ u. Say them like Spanish or Italian vowels: ე is never "ay" as in *day*, ო is never "oh" as in *go* – no glide at the end.
- The letters "sit" on a line; some have ascenders or descenders. Pay attention to the shape, not the size.

New today: მ m, ნ n, ლ l, ს s (always voiceless as in *sun*, never like the *s* in *is*).

## Pitfall

**მამა** (mama) means **father**, not mother! Mother is დედა (deda) – that comes in A0-02.

## Plan (about 30 min)

1. App → Letters: listen to each letter, repeat it, record yourself. (10 min)
2. App → letter quiz until you get 90 % right. (5 min)
3. App → read the words and do the flashcards. (10 min)
4. App → type with the on-screen keyboard: მამა, ლომი, სამი. (5 min)

## For Claude (chat lesson)

Reading practice with syllables such as მა, ნო, ლი, სუ, then the words. Quiz in both directions. Check that the learner reliably tells ი and ო apart, and that ე/ო stay pure vowels without an English glide.

lessons.title: Voiced sounds, the rolled r and h
lessons.body:
## What this is about

New letters: ბ b · გ g · დ d · ვ v · ზ z · რ r · ჰ h

Three things to watch as an English speaker:

1. **Voiced stays voiced.** ბ, გ, დ are fully voiced, even at the end of a word – don't let them fade into p, k, t. ვარდი (vardi) has a clear voiced d.
2. **ზ is the English z** (as in *zoo*) – easy. ლამაზი = la-ma-**z**i. And ს from A0-01 is always s, never z.
3. **რ is rolled or tapped with the tip of the tongue** (as in Spanish or Scottish English), never the English *r* where the tongue curls back without touching: ორი = o-**r**-i, a quick tap.

ვ is roughly English *v*, ჰ is the *h* in *hat*.

## Words

From now on you can already read real little sentences: **დედა და მამა** – mother and father. **ის ლამაზი გოგო** – that beautiful girl.

## Plan (about 30 min)

1. Listen to the letters and repeat them; practise რ in particular. (8 min)
2. Quiz, including review of A0-01. (7 min)
3. Words and flashcards. (10 min)
4. Typing: დედა, ორი, ლამაზი. (5 min)

## For Claude (chat lesson)

Build short reading sentences from known words. Introduce questions with რა? and ვინ? (ვინ არის? comes later; here only as a word).

lessons.title: Breath or click – t, p, k in two versions each
lessons.body:
## What this is about – the most important pronunciation rule of Georgian

Georgian has **two** sounds each for t, p and k:

| aspirated (like English) | ejective (new!) |
|---|---|
| თ t – as in *top* | ტ t' |
| ფ p – as in *pot* | პ p' |
| ქ k – as in *kit* | კ k' |

**Aspirated**: you already say these correctly – like English p, t, k at the start of a word, with a small puff of air.
**Ejective**: no puff of air. Instead the larynx (voice box) closes briefly and you get a hard "click" or "pop".

### How to learn ejectives

1. Hold a sheet of paper in front of your mouth. With თ/ფ/ქ it moves, with ტ/პ/კ it doesn't.
2. Hold your breath briefly, as if about to lift a heavy box. While holding your breath, say "k". That is კ.
3. Say "ka" while holding your breath: კა. The "a" starts hard, almost with a pop.

Useful intermediate step: the p in *spin*, the t in *stop* and the k in *skin* have no puff of air. That is not yet an ejective, but it is closer than *pin*, *top*, *kin*.

### It changes the meaning!

- **ქარი** (kari) = wind · **კარი** (k'ari) = door
- **ფური** (puri) = cow · **პური** (p'uri) = bread

Watch the keyboard: ფ is on the **f** key, but it is **not an f** – it is an aspirated p.

## Plan (about 30 min)

1. Listen to the letters; minimal pairs in listening practice. (10 min)
2. Record yourself: ქარი/კარი, ფური/პური – compare with the original each time. (8 min)
3. Words and flashcards. (8 min)
4. Typing: თბილისი, ქართული. (4 min)

## For Claude (chat lesson)

Focus on the minimal pairs. Many learners at first simply say ejectives without aspiration (like *spin*, or "like French"); that is a good intermediate step, but work towards the click.

lessons.title: ts, dz, ch, j – affricates in three versions
lessons.body:
## What this is about

The same principle as in A0-03, now with "ts" and "ch", each with a voiced partner as well:

| aspirated | ejective | voiced |
|---|---|---|
| ც ts (as in *cats*) | წ ts' | ძ dz (as in *kids*) |
| ჩ ch (as in *church*) | ჭ ch' | ჯ j (as in *jam*) |

Good news for English speakers: in the transliteration **ch is the English ch** and **j is the English j**. Note that ც (ts) can also stand at the start of a word, where English never has it: ცივი (tsivi) – practise saying *ts* + *i* without a vowel in between.

## Words

**კაცი და ქალი** – man and woman. **ჩაი, ცივი წყალი…** (you learn წყალი in A0-05).

## Plan (about 30 min)

1. Listen to the letters and repeat them. (8 min)
2. Listening practice ც/წ and ჩ/ჭ. (7 min)
3. Words and flashcards (including review of A0-03). (10 min)
4. Typing: წიგნი, ბიჭი. (5 min)

## For Claude (chat lesson)

Weave in review of the ejectives from A0-03. Review the numbers 1, 2, 3, 10, 100 (ერთი, ორი, სამი, ათი, ასი).

lessons.title: sh, zh and the back sounds kh, gh, q'
lessons.body:
## What this is about

The last five letters. After this you can **read any Georgian word**.

- შ sh – as in *shoe*
- ჟ zh – the voiced sh, like the *s* in *measure* or *vision*
- ხ kh – as in Scottish *loch* or German *Bach*, a rough friction at the back of the mouth. **Never** a plain k or h.
- ღ gh – the voiced partner of ხ: a strong, rubbed sound at the back of the throat, close to the French or German *r* (as in French *Paris*). Careful: Georgian რ, by contrast, is rolled with the tongue tip!
- ყ q' – an ejective right at the back, near the uvula. Like კ, only further back in the throat. The hardest sound; don't let it discourage you.

## Numbers 1–10 complete

ერთი 1 · ორი 2 · სამი 3 · ოთხი 4 · ხუთი 5 · ექვსი 6 · შვიდი 7 · რვა 8 · ცხრა 9 · ათი 10

## Words for your first visit

ყავა coffee · ჩაი tea · წყალი water · ღვინო wine · პური bread · ყველი cheese · ხაჭაპური khachapuri

## Plan (about 30 min)

1. Listen to the letters; compare ხ/ღ and კ/ყ. (10 min)
2. Numbers 1–10 as flashcards. (8 min)
3. Words and flashcards. (7 min)
4. Typing: წყალი, ხაჭაპური. (5 min)

## For Claude (chat lesson)

Review the whole alphabet (quiz on all 33). Numbers 1–10 in both directions.

lessons.title: Consonant clusters, stress, reading fluently
lessons.body:
## What this is about

**Consonant clusters**: Georgian loves consonants in a row: მწვრთნელი (mts'vrtneli, coach), გვფრცქვნი (gvprtskvni, 8 consonants!). Trick: slowly from left to right, every sound on its own, with no helper vowel in between – then speed up.

**Stress**: weak, and it never changes the meaning. Mostly on the first syllable; in longer words often on the third from last. Better to say all syllables evenly than to impose a strong English stress pattern – and don't reduce unstressed vowels to a vague "uh": every ა stays a.

**From now on the transliteration is hidden.** You can show it with a tap, but try without.

## Your first sentences

- გამარჯობა! – Hello!
- გმადლობთ. – Thank you.
- ნახვამდის! – Goodbye!

## Plan (about 30 min)

1. Reading practice: city names and long words, out loud, with recording. (12 min)
2. Full review of all A0 cards. (13 min)
3. Typing without transliteration. (5 min)

## End of A0

You can read, type and pronounce all 33 letters. Next comes A1 (greetings, "to be", pronouns).

lessons.title: Greetings and introductions
lessons.body:
## What this is about

The first sentences for every encounter: greeting, asking how someone is, exchanging names, being polite. The usual reply to გამარჯობა is გაგიმარჯოს – not obligatory, but it sounds very natural.

## Dialogue (by Claude, not yet checked)

- გამარჯობა! – Hello!
- გაგიმარჯოს! რა გქვია? – Hello! What's your name?
- თომასი მქვია. შენ? – My name is Thomas. And you?
- ნინო მქვია. როგორ ხარ? – My name is Nino. How are you?
- კარგად, მადლობა. – Fine, thanks.
- ნახვამდის! – Goodbye!

## Grammar in brief

- "My name is" = მქვია, "your name is" = გქვია, "his/her name is" = ჰქვია – the person is in the prefix. Literally it is closer to "(it) is called to me".
- Polite (formal "you") and plural: გქვიათ, გთხოვთ, გაგიმარჯოთ.

In detail: grammar chapter `g-heissen`.

## Plan (about 30 min)

1. Review (cards due). (5 min)
2. Read the dialogue and repeat it aloud, with audio. (5 min)
3. Read the grammar in brief (g-heissen). (5 min)
4. New words: flashcards in both directions. (10 min)
5. Sentences: cloze / typing. (5 min)

## In the chat (/lektion)

Role-play a greeting: Claude is a Georgian woman in a café, you introduce yourself.

Move on when the quiz is ≥ 90 % on two days.

lessons.title: Pronouns and "to be"
goals: I am / you are / he is …
lessons.body:
## What this is about

The most important verb: "to be". Georgian pronouns have no gender – ის means he, she and it. Instead there are three levels of "this/that", depending on distance.

## Dialogue (by Claude, not yet checked)

- ეს ვინ არის? – Who is this?
- ეს ჩემი ძმაა. – This is my brother.
- ის სტუდენტია? – Is he a student?
- არა, ის ექიმია. – No, he is a doctor.

## Grammar in brief

- ვარ, ხარ, არის, ვართ, ხართ, არიან – the verb usually comes at the end.
- Instead of არის often just -ა: ეს გოგოა = ეს არის გოგო.
- თქვენ is also the polite "you" (like French *vous*), with the verb in the plural.
- There are no articles: ექიმი = "doctor", "a doctor" or "the doctor".

In detail: grammar chapters `g-pronomen`, `g-kopula`.

## Plan (about 30 min)

1. Review (cards due). (5 min)
2. Read the dialogue and repeat it aloud, with audio. (5 min)
3. Read the grammar in brief (g-pronomen, g-kopula). (5 min)
4. New words: flashcards in both directions. (10 min)
5. Sentences: cloze / typing. (5 min)

## In the chat (/lektion)

Describing people: "Who is this?" – Claude names people, you answer with ვარ/ხარ/არის.

Move on when the quiz is ≥ 90 % on two days.

lessons.title: Who are you? Origin, job, questions
goals: say where you are from and what you do
lessons.body:
## What this is about

Now you can say who you are and where you come from – and ask the other person. Questions work by intonation alone; the word order stays the same and there is no "do".

## Dialogue (by Claude, not yet checked)

- შენ ქართველი ხარ? – Are you Georgian?
- არა, გერმანელი ვარ. შენ? – No, I'm German. And you?
- მე ქართველი ვარ. სტუდენტი ხარ? – I'm Georgian. Are you a student?
- არა, მასწავლებელი ვარ. – No, I'm a teacher.
- ეს შენი მეგობარია? – Is this your friend?
- კი, ჩემი მეგობარია. – Yes, that's my friend.

## Grammar in brief

- Yes/no question = statement with rising intonation.
- არ goes directly before the verb: არ ვარ – I am not.
- -ელი = "person from …": გერმანელი (German), ქართველი (Georgian); likewise ინგლისელი (English), ამერიკელი (American).

In detail: grammar chapters `g-fragen-verneinung`, `g-kopula`, `g-possessiva`.

## Plan (about 30 min)

1. Review (cards due). (5 min)
2. Read the dialogue and repeat it aloud, with audio. (5 min)
3. Read the grammar in brief (g-fragen-verneinung, g-kopula, g-possessiva). (5 min)
4. New words: flashcards in both directions. (10 min)
5. Sentences: cloze / typing. (5 min)

## In the chat (/lektion)

Getting-to-know-you interview: Claude asks you questions (name, origin, job), then the other way round.

Move on when the quiz is ≥ 90 % on two days.

lessons.title: Numbers 0–20
goals: understand the time on the full hour
lessons.body:
## What this is about

From eleven to nineteen there is a pattern: "ten-X-more" (თ- … -მეტი). If you know the numbers 1–10 from A0, this is easy – apart from two exceptions.

## Dialogue (by Claude, not yet checked)

- რამდენი წლის ხარ? – How old are you?
- ცხრამეტი წლის ვარ. – I'm nineteen.
- რომელი საათია? – What time is it?
- თორმეტი საათია. – It's twelve o'clock.

## Grammar in brief

- 11–19: თ- + number + -მეტი; exceptions ცამეტი (13), ჩვიდმეტი (17).
- After numbers the noun stays in the singular: სამი ბავშვი – literally "three child".

In detail: grammar chapter `g-zahlen`.

## Plan (about 30 min)

1. Review (cards due). (5 min)
2. Read the dialogue and repeat it aloud, with audio. (5 min)
3. Read the grammar in brief (g-zahlen). (5 min)
4. New words: flashcards in both directions. (10 min)
5. Sentences: cloze / typing. (5 min)

## In the chat (/lektion)

Number ping-pong: Claude says a number in English, you answer in Georgian (and the other way round).

Move on when the quiz is ≥ 90 % on two days.

lessons.title: Numbers up to 100, age and prices
lessons.body:
## What this is about

Georgian counts in twenties – like the old English "score" (*four score and seven*) or French *quatre-vingts*, only consistently: 50 = 2 × 20 + 10. With one simple rule you can then build any number up to 99.

## Dialogue (by Claude, not yet checked)

- ეს რა ღირს? – How much is this?
- ოცდახუთი ლარი. – Twenty-five lari.
- რამდენი? – How much?
- ოცდახუთი. ოცი და ხუთი. – Twenty-five. Twenty and five.

## Grammar in brief

- 30 = 20 + 10, 40 = 2 × 20, 60 = 3 × 20, 80 = 4 × 20.
- In between: the twenty-word without -ი + და + 1–19: ოცდაერთი (21), სამოცდაცამეტი (73 = 3 × 20 + 13).
- Age: X წლის ვარ – I am X years old.
- Money: 1 lari (ლარი) = 100 tetri (თეთრი).

In detail: grammar chapter `g-zahlen`.

## Plan (about 30 min)

1. Review (cards due). (5 min)
2. Read the dialogue and repeat it aloud, with audio. (5 min)
3. Read the grammar in brief (g-zahlen). (5 min)
4. New words: flashcards in both directions. (10 min)
5. Sentences: cloze / typing. (5 min)

## In the chat (/lektion)

Market game: Claude names prices, you add them up and say the total in Georgian.

Move on when the quiz is ≥ 90 % on two days.

lessons.title: Nominative, dative and "to have"
lessons.body:
## What this is about

The dative (-ს) is the workhorse case of Georgian. And "to have" works like "to me there is …": the owner in the dative, the thing in the nominative. For people, animals and cars there is a separate verb.

## Dialogue (by Claude, not yet checked)

- მანქანა გყავს? – Do you have a car?
- არა, მანქანა არ მყავს. შენ? – No, I don't have a car. You?
- მე ძველი მანქანა მყავს. – I have an old car.
- ბავშვები გყავს? – Do you have children?
- კი, ორი ბავშვი მყავს. – Yes, I have two children.
- დრო გაქვს? – Do you have time?
- ახლა არა. – Not now.

## Grammar in brief

- Dative: -ი → -ს (სახლი → სახლს), vowel + -ს (დედა → დედას). ის → მას, ისინი → მათ.
- მაქვს/გაქვს/აქვს for things, მყავს/გყავს/ჰყავს for living beings and cars.

In detail: grammar chapters `g-kasus-nom-dat`, `g-haben`.

## Plan (about 30 min)

1. Review (cards due). (5 min)
2. Read the dialogue and repeat it aloud, with audio. (5 min)
3. Read the grammar in brief (g-kasus-nom-dat, g-haben). (5 min)
4. New words: flashcards in both directions. (10 min)
5. Sentences: cloze / typing. (5 min)

## In the chat (/lektion)

What do you have? Claude asks about things and people, you answer with მაქვს/მყავს.

Move on when the quiz is ≥ 90 % on two days.

lessons.title: Where? -ში, -ზე, -თან
lessons.body:
## What this is about

Georgian attaches "in", "on" and "at" to the end of the word – to the dative without -ს. The same ending answers both "where?" and "where to?".

## Dialogue (by Claude, not yet checked)

- სად ხარ? – Where are you?
- სამსახურში ვარ. შენ? – At work. And you?
- მე მაღაზიაში ვარ. – I'm in the shop.
- დედა სად არის? – Where is Mum?
- დედა ექიმთან არის. – Mum is at the doctor's.

## Grammar in brief

- -ში in, -ზე on, -თან at/by: სახლში, მაგიდაზე, ექიმთან.
- Short form: მაღაზიაშია – is in the shop.

In detail: grammar chapter `g-postpositionen`.

## Plan (about 30 min)

1. Review (cards due). (5 min)
2. Read the dialogue and repeat it aloud, with audio. (5 min)
3. Read the grammar in brief (g-postpositionen). (5 min)
4. New words: flashcards in both directions. (10 min)
5. Sentences: cloze / typing. (5 min)

## In the chat (/lektion)

Picture puzzle: Claude describes a room ("The book is on the table …"), you ask with სად.

Move on when the quiz is ≥ 90 % on two days.

lessons.title: Present tense: live, work, speak
goals: conjugate regular verbs in the present
say where you live and work
lessons.body:
## What this is about

The first action verbs. The system is simple: ვ- for "I", -ს for "he/she", -თ for the plural. The object is in the dative. Georgian has one present tense for both "I live" and "I am living".

## Dialogue (by Claude, not yet checked)

- სად ცხოვრობ? – Where do you live?
- თბილისში ვცხოვრობ. – I live in Tbilisi.
- სად მუშაობ? – Where do you work?
- სკოლაში ვმუშაობ. მასწავლებელი ვარ. – I work at a school. I'm a teacher.
- ქართულად ლაპარაკობ? – Do you speak Georgian?
- ცოტა. ქართულს ვსწავლობ. – A little. I'm learning Georgian.

## Grammar in brief

- ვცხოვრობ – ცხოვრობ – ცხოვრობს – ვცხოვრობთ – ცხოვრობთ – ცხოვრობენ.
- Object in the dative: წიგნს ვკითხულობ, წყალს ვსვამ.
- "in Georgian" = ქართულად, "in German" = გერმანულად (likewise ინგლისურად – in English).

In detail: grammar chapter `g-praesens`.

## Plan (about 30 min)

1. Review (cards due). (5 min)
2. Read the dialogue and repeat it aloud, with audio. (5 min)
3. Read the grammar in brief (g-praesens). (5 min)
4. New words: flashcards in both directions. (10 min)
5. Sentences: cloze / typing. (5 min)

## In the chat (/lektion)

Daily routine: Claude asks what you are doing (რას აკეთებ?), you answer with the new verbs.

Move on when the quiz is ≥ 90 % on two days.

lessons.title: Want, like, can
lessons.body:
## What this is about

For feelings Georgian says "to me it is …" – like with მაქვს: the person is a prefix (მ-, გ-, …), the thing wanted is in the nominative. Compare English "it pleases me" instead of "I like it". With these verbs you get a long way in everyday life.

## Dialogue (by Claude, not yet checked)

- რა გინდა? – What would you like?
- ყავა მინდა. შენ? – I'd like coffee. And you?
- მე ჩაი მინდა. ქართული ჩაი მომწონს. – I'd like tea. I like Georgian tea.
- რატომ? – Why?
- არ ვიცი. უბრალოდ მომწონს. – I don't know. I just like it.

## Grammar in brief

- მ- = to me, გ- = to you, გვ- = to us; 3rd person irregular (უნდა, უყვარს, მოსწონს, სჭირდება).
- ვიცი (I know) is a normal verb.

In detail: grammar chapter `g-dativverben`.

## Plan (about 30 min)

1. Review (cards due). (5 min)
2. Read the dialogue and repeat it aloud, with audio. (5 min)
3. Read the grammar in brief (g-dativverben). (5 min)
4. New words: flashcards in both directions. (10 min)
5. Sentences: cloze / typing. (5 min)

## In the chat (/lektion)

Likes: Claude names things, you say მომწონს / არ მომწონს / მიყვარს.

Move on when the quiz is ≥ 90 % on two days.

lessons.title: Family and possessives
lessons.body:
## What this is about

Family matters a great deal in Georgia – expect questions about children and parents. Possessives come before the noun; with close relatives they are often attached at the end: დედაჩემი (my mother).

## Dialogue (by Claude, not yet checked)

- ოჯახი გყავს? – Do you have a family?
- კი. ცოლი და ორი შვილი მყავს. – Yes. A wife and two children.
- ვაჟი და ქალიშვილი? – A son and a daughter?
- ორი ქალიშვილი. – Two daughters.
- შენი მშობლები სად ცხოვრობენ? – Where do your parents live?
- ჩემი მშობლები გერმანიაში ცხოვრობენ. – My parents live in Germany.

## Grammar in brief

- ჩემი, შენი, მისი, ჩვენი, თქვენი, მათი – before the noun; in the dative ჩემს.
- მისი means both "his" and "her".
- დედაჩემი, მამაჩემი – very common.

In detail: grammar chapter `g-possessiva`.

## Plan (about 30 min)

1. Review (cards due). (5 min)
2. Read the dialogue and repeat it aloud, with audio. (5 min)
3. Read the grammar in brief (g-possessiva). (5 min)
4. New words: flashcards in both directions. (10 min)
5. Sentences: cloze / typing. (5 min)

## In the chat (/lektion)

Family tree: you describe your family, Claude asks follow-up questions.

Move on when the quiz is ≥ 90 % on two days.

lessons.title: Food and drink
goals: say you are hungry or thirsty
lessons.body:
## What this is about

Georgian hospitality means: you will eat a lot. Hunger and thirst are dative verbs like მინდა: მშია – literally "to me it hungers".

## Dialogue (by Claude, not yet checked)

- გშია? – Are you hungry?
- კი, ძალიან მშია! – Yes, very hungry!
- ხაჭაპური გინდა? – Would you like khachapuri?
- კი, და ერთი წვენი, გთხოვთ. – Yes, and a juice, please.
- გემრიელია? – Is it good?
- ძალიან გემრიელია! – Very tasty!

## Grammar in brief

- მშია / მწყურია follow the pattern of მინდა: გშია?, შია, გვშია …
- Ordering: X, გთხოვთ / X მინდა.

In detail: grammar chapter `g-dativverben`.

## Plan (about 30 min)

1. Review (cards due). (5 min)
2. Read the dialogue and repeat it aloud, with audio. (5 min)
3. Read the grammar in brief (g-dativverben). (5 min)
4. New words: flashcards in both directions. (10 min)
5. Sentences: cloze / typing. (5 min)

## In the chat (/lektion)

At the restaurant: Claude is the waiter or waitress, you order and ask questions.

Move on when the quiz is ≥ 90 % on two days.

lessons.title: Days of the week and telling the time
lessons.body:
## What this is about

Four weekdays are counted from Saturday (შაბათი): ორშაბათი "two after Saturday" = Monday, სამშაბათი = Tuesday, and so on. "On Monday" is simply the dative (ორშაბათს), "at three o'clock" is სამ საათზე.

## Dialogue (by Claude, not yet checked)

- დღეს რა დღეა? – What day is it today?
- დღეს პარასკევია. – Today is Friday.
- რომელი საათია? – What time is it?
- ახლა ხუთი საათია. – It's five o'clock now.
- ხვალ სამსახურში ხარ? – Are you at work tomorrow?
- არა, ხვალ შაბათია – სახლში ვარ. – No, tomorrow is Saturday – I'm at home.

## Grammar in brief

- ორშაბათი … კვირა; on a day: dative ორშაბათს.
- რომელი საათია? – X საათია. At X: X (without -ი) საათზე.

In detail: grammar chapters `g-zeit`, `g-postpositionen`.

## Plan (about 30 min)

1. Review (cards due). (5 min)
2. Read the dialogue and repeat it aloud, with audio. (5 min)
3. Read the grammar in brief (g-zeit, g-postpositionen). (5 min)
4. New words: flashcards in both directions. (10 min)
5. Sentences: cloze / typing. (5 min)

## In the chat (/lektion)

Weekly plan: Claude asks when you do what; you answer with the day and time.

Move on when the quiz is ≥ 90 % on two days.

lessons.title: Directions and transport
lessons.body:
## What this is about

With მი- (away, "there") and მო- (towards, "here") the verb shows the direction from the speaker's point of view – a bit like English *go* vs *come*. Plus the most important words for directions in Tbilisi.

## Dialogue (by Claude, not yet checked)

- ბოდიში, სად არის მეტრო? – Excuse me, where is the metro?
- პირდაპირ, მერე მარჯვნივ. – Straight on, then right.
- შორსაა? – Is it far?
- არა, ახლოსაა. – No, it's close.
- სად მიდიხარ? – Where are you going?
- სახლში მივდივარ. – I'm going home.

## Grammar in brief

- მივდივარ (I go, I'm going there) – მოვდივარ (I come, I'm coming).
- -დან = from: სახლიდან; -მდე = up to, as far as: სადგურამდე.

In detail: grammar chapters `g-bewegung`, `g-postpositionen`.

## Plan (about 30 min)

1. Review (cards due). (5 min)
2. Read the dialogue and repeat it aloud, with audio. (5 min)
3. Read the grammar in brief (g-bewegung, g-postpositionen). (5 min)
4. New words: flashcards in both directions. (10 min)
5. Sentences: cloze / typing. (5 min)

## In the chat (/lektion)

Map game: Claude describes a route, you say where you end up – and the other way round.

Move on when the quiz is ≥ 90 % on two days.

lessons.title: Plural, colours and adjectives
lessons.body:
## What this is about

The plural is regular: -ები. Adjectives come before the noun and stay in the singular there, just as in English: დიდი სახლები – big houses. After numbers and ბევრი (many) there is no plural.

## Dialogue (by Claude, not yet checked)

- ეს შენი მანქანაა? – Is this your car?
- არა, ჩემი მანქანა შავია. ეს მწვანეა. – No, my car is black. This one is green.
- ბევრი მეგობარი გყავს? – Do you have many friends?
- კი, ჩემი მეგობრები ქართველები არიან. – Yes, my friends are Georgian.

## Grammar in brief

- სახლი → სახლები, მანქანა → მანქანები, მეგობარი → მეგობრები.
- დიდი სახლები (adjective without plural), ბევრი მეგობარი (singular – literally "many friend").

In detail: grammar chapter `g-plural`.

## Plan (about 30 min)

1. Review (cards due). (5 min)
2. Read the dialogue and repeat it aloud, with audio. (5 min)
3. Read the grammar in brief (g-plural). (5 min)
4. New words: flashcards in both directions. (10 min)
5. Sentences: cloze / typing. (5 min)

## In the chat (/lektion)

Describing: Claude shows things (in words), you describe colour and size – also in the plural.

Move on when the quiz is ≥ 90 % on two days.

lessons.title: Shopping and end of A1
lessons.body:
## What this is about

To round off A1, everything together: numbers, prices, wishes, polite forms. At the market (ბაზარი) people like to haggle – ძალიან ძვირია! (too expensive!) helps.

## Dialogue (by Claude, not yet checked)

- გამარჯობა! ვაშლი რა ღირს? – Hello! How much are the apples?
- კილო – სამი ლარი. – Three lari a kilo.
- ძალიან ძვირია! – That's very expensive!
- კარგი, ორი ლარი და ორმოცდაათი თეთრი. – All right, two lari fifty.
- ორი კილო მომეცით, გთხოვთ. – Two kilos, please.
- ხუთი ლარი. ხურდა გაქვთ? – Five lari. Do you have change?
- კი. მადლობა, ნახვამდის! – Yes. Thank you, goodbye!

## Grammar in brief

- Quantities: ერთი კილო ვაშლი, ორი ბოთლი წყალი – noun in the singular, no "of".
- Polite: მომეცით, გთხოვთ, გაქვთ.

In detail: grammar chapters `g-zahlen`, `g-dativverben`, `g-kasus-nom-dat`.

## Plan (about 30 min)

1. Review (cards due). (5 min)
2. Read the dialogue and repeat it aloud, with audio. (5 min)
3. Read the grammar in brief (g-zahlen, g-dativverben, g-kasus-nom-dat). (5 min)
4. New words: flashcards in both directions. (10 min)
5. Sentences: cloze / typing. (5 min)

## In the chat (/lektion)

Market role-play: Claude sells, you buy and haggle. Then the A1 final quiz.

Move on when the quiz is ≥ 90 % on two days.
